sections.title: Basic Concept of Input Output
sections.content: In Input Output questions, some words or numbers are given in a sequence. A machine rearranges them in each step according to a fixed rule. After every step, a new arrangement is formed which is called Step 1, Step 2, and so on. Our task is to understand the rule used by the machine and predict the next arrangement.

sections.title: What is Single-End Shifting
sections.content:
In Single-End Shifting, the machine places only one element in its correct position in each step. This process starts either from the left side or the right side. Example: Input: 8 3 6 1
Step 1: 1 8 3 6
Step 2: 1 3 8 6
Step 3: 1 3 6 8
Here the smallest number moves to its correct position on the left side in each step.

sections.title: Number Sorting
sections.content:
In number sorting, numbers are arranged either in ascending order (smallest to largest) or descending order (largest to smallest). Example:
Input: 7 2 9 4
Ascending: 2 4 7 9
Descending: 9 7 4 2
The machine places one number in its correct position in each step.

sections.title: Word Sorting
sections.content:
In word sorting, words are arranged in alphabetical order. In English, the order is from A to Z. Example:
Input: Mango Apple Banana
Step 1: Apple Mango Banana
Step 2: Apple Banana Mango
In Hindi, the order is based on vowels and consonants such as अ, आ, इ, ई, उ, etc.

sections.title: Identifying Step-Based Patterns
sections.content: The most important task in Input Output problems is identifying the pattern. Carefully observe the Input, Step 1, and Step 2. Identify which element has moved to its final position. Usually, only one element reaches its correct position in each step.

sections.title: Questions Asked in Exams
sections.content:
1. What will happen after Step 2
2. Which element will change in Step 3
3. What will be the final output
4. Which element will be present in a particular step

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1. Not checking whether sorting is happening from the left or the right side.
2. Confusing ascending and descending order.
3. Misunderstanding alphabetical order.
4. Guessing the rule without properly analyzing the step pattern.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Input Output questions, a machine rearranges elements in each step according to a rule. Most problems use sorting, shifting, or alphabetical order. The most important skill is identifying the rule by observing the input and the initial steps.

tricks.title: Check the First and Last Element
tricks.explanation: Often in Step 1, the smallest or largest element moves to its correct position. This helps identify the direction of sorting.
tricks.example:
Input: 8 5 2 9
Step 1: 2 8 5 9 → The smallest number comes first.

tricks.title: Identify Left-Side Sorting
tricks.explanation: If in each step a new correct element is added on the left side, then sorting is happening from the left.

tricks.title: Identify Right-Side Sorting
tricks.explanation: If in each step the correct element appears on the right side, then sorting is happening from the right.

tricks.title: Remember Alphabetical Order
tricks.explanation: Arrange words from A to Z. Always check the first letter.
tricks.example:
Input: Dog Apple Cat
Final: Apple Cat Dog

tricks.title: Understand Hindi Word Order
tricks.explanation: Hindi words are arranged according to the order of letters like अ, आ, इ, ई, उ, etc.
tricks.example:
Input: आम इमली अनार
Final: अनार आम इमली

tricks.title: One Change Per Step Rule
tricks.explanation: In Level 1 problems, usually only one element reaches its final position in each step.

tricks.title: Identify Step Pattern Quickly
tricks.explanation: Compare the Input and Step 1 to see which element changed position.
tricks.example:
Input: 7 2 6 4
Step 1: 2 7 6 4 → The smallest number moves forward.

tricks.title: Ascending vs Descending Identification
tricks.explanation: If the smallest number appears first, it is ascending order. If the largest appears first, it is descending order.

tricks.title: Identify Final Output Quickly
tricks.explanation: If the rule is sorting, the final output will be a completely sorted list.

tricks.title: Identify Number of Steps
tricks.explanation: If there are n elements and one element is fixed in each step, the final output usually appears in about n-1 steps.
